description:
A quality-gate verdict reflects the change under review rather than what else the host was doing while the gate ran.

## Background

`cargo-ci` is the authoritative gate for Rust changes, and it is not deterministic under host load. `crates/server/tests/server_integration/graceful_shutdown_tests.rs::test_jit_server_shutdown_force_closes_a_stalled_connection_and_exits_zero` failed a gate with "the stalled connection was dropped before the drain deadline" at load average 6–10, with a concurrent build running beside the gate. It passes repeatedly on an idle host.

The consequence is procedural as well as technical: every issue's verdict becomes load-dependent, and the operational workaround adopted during the last container was to serialise all work behind the gate, which costs wall-clock on every issue in every wave.

A timing-sensitive assertion inside the authoritative whole-workspace gate is the problem; whether the fix is a different assertion, an injected clock, or moving the property to a suite that is not the blocking gate is a design question.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The drain property is asserted in a way whose outcome does not change with unrelated load on the host.
- [hard] REQ-02: The assertion still fails when the behaviour it protects actually regresses, demonstrated against a seeded regression.
- [hard] REQ-03: `cargo-ci` produces the same verdict for one tree whether or not another build runs concurrently.
title: Make the cargo-ci verdict independent of unrelated host load
